source.text: Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα περιεπάτει ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ, οὐ γὰρ ἤθελεν ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ περιπατεῖν, ὅτι ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἀποκτεῖναι.

records.literal_gloss: And after these things was walking the Jesus in the Galilee; for not he was wanting in the Judea to walk, because were seeking him the Jews to kill.

en.L: And after these things Jesus was walking about in Galilee, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not want to walk about in Judea, because the Jews were seeking to kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: After this Jesus went from place to place in Galilee. He did not want to travel around Judea, because the Jewish leaders there were looking for a way to kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: After this, Jesus traveled around Galilee. He did not want to go around Judea, because the Jewish leaders there were trying to kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y después de estas cosas, Jesús andaba por Galilea, pues no quería andar por Judea, porque los judíos buscaban matarlo.
es.B: Después de esto, Jesús andaba de un lugar a otro por Galilea. No quería recorrer Judea, porque allí los dirigentes judíos buscaban la manera de matarlo.
es.R: Después de esto, Jesús viajaba por Galilea. No quería ir por Judea, porque allí los dirigentes judíos querían matarlo.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the religious authorities in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: They are the ones already seeking to kill Jesus in 5:18, and the same aim returns in 7:19 and 7:25. That is the leadership, not the people of Judea as a whole: Jesus, his brothers and his disciples are Jews, and the crowds in Jerusalem are divided about him (7:12).

decisions.choice: he did not want (SBLGNT)
alternatives: he did not have authority (a few witnesses)
decisions.reason: The reading of almost all manuscripts is "he did not want" to travel in Judea. A few witnesses, among them Codex Washingtonianus (W) and some early Latin copies, read "he did not have authority" (that is, he was not free) to travel there. The change may have come from a wish to show that Jesus was not avoiding danger out of fear. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: was walking about: a period of travel in Galilee, some months long
decisions.reason: The tense describes an ongoing ministry from place to place. "After these things" covers a gap: chapter 6 took place near Passover (6:4), in spring, and the Feast of Tabernacles (7:2) came in autumn, about six months later. The verb "walk" is used again for Judea, so the two regions stand side by side.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}}, {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for Christ uses the deity_pronoun setting, including "me" and "my" when Jesus speaks of himself and "you" and "your" when his brothers speak to him. At the start of a sentence "He" or "My" is written plain. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: the Jewish leaders there
decisions.reason: Where the word means the authorities, Balanced and Readable name them (see the book's terms). The footnote gives the word John wrote. "There" ties them to Judea, where Jesus is not going.

decisions.choice: los judíos (L); los dirigentes judíos (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the religious authorities in Jerusalem (meaning decision m1), so Balanced and Readable name them, as at 5:10-18. The word John wrote is "los judíos".

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros; deity_pronoun on stressed pronouns
decisions.reason: As throughout John: every plural "you" is the ustedes / vosotros reader setting, and the deity_pronoun setting is on stressed pronouns for Christ (él, tú, mí, sí).

source.text: ἦν δὲ ἐγγὺς ἡ ἑορτὴ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἡ σκηνοπηγία.

records.literal_gloss: Now was near the feast of the Jews, the Tabernacles.

en.L: Now the feast of the Jews, the [Feast of] Tabernacles, was near.
en.B: Now the Jewish Festival of Tabernacles was near.
en.R: It was almost time for the Jewish Festival of Shelters. For a week each year, people lived in shelters made of branches. This helped them remember how God cared for Israel in the desert.

es.L: Y estaba cerca la fiesta de los judíos, la de los Tabernáculos.
es.B: Se acercaba la fiesta judía de los Tabernáculos.
es.R: Faltaba poco para la fiesta judía de las Enramadas. Cada año, durante una semana, el pueblo vivía en enramadas hechas con ramas. Así recordaban cómo Dios había cuidado a Israel en el desierto.

decisions.choice: Tabernacles: the autumn festival when Israel lived in shelters
decisions.reason: The name σκηνοπηγία means "the setting up of tents" or shelters. The Law commanded Israel to keep the festival for seven days in the seventh month, after the harvest of grain and grapes had been gathered in, and to live in shelters of branches to remember that God made Israel live in shelters when he brought them out of Egypt (Leviticus 23:33-43; Deuteronomy 16:13-15; Nehemiah 8:14-17). It was one of the three festivals when men were to go up to the place God chose (Deuteronomy 16:16), so Jerusalem filled with pilgrims. It was a joyful feast. Jewish writings from soon after the New Testament (the Mishnah, tractate Sukkah) describe water being poured out at the altar and great lamps lit in the temple courts during the festival; Jesus's words about living water and light in 7:37-38 and 8:12 are spoken at this feast.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the Jewish people, whose festival it was
decisions.reason: As at 2:13, 5:1 and 6:4, John names the festival as the people's, for readers who did not keep it. Jesus and his brothers are Jews and go up to keep it (7:10).

decisions.choice: Tabernacles (L, B); Festival of Shelters (R)
decisions.reason: "Tabernacles" is the long-established name of the festival and is kept at Literal and Balanced. In current speech "tabernacle" mostly means the tent of meeting, so Readable uses the plain word "shelters". Balanced says "festival" for the feast, as at 5:1 and 6:4.

decisions.choice: For a week each year ... cared for Israel in the desert
decisions.reason: Readable says what the festival was, as 6:4 does for Passover (meaning decision m1). The reason given is the one Leviticus 23:43 states.

decisions.choice: los Tabernáculos (L, B); las Enramadas (R)
decisions.reason: "Tabernáculos" is the long-established name and is kept at Literal and Balanced. Readable says "Enramadas", the plain word for shelters made of branches (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Cada año, durante una semana ... en el desierto
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says what the festival was.

source.text: εἶπον οὖν πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ· Μετάβηθι ἐντεῦθεν καὶ ὕπαγε εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν, ἵνα καὶ οἱ μαθηταί σου θεωρήσουσιν σοῦ τὰ ἔργα ἃ ποιεῖς·

records.literal_gloss: Said therefore to him the brothers of him, "Move from here and go into the Judea, so that also the disciples of you will see of you the works which you do;

en.L: So {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} brothers said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Move on from here and go into Judea, so that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples also will see {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} works that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are doing;
en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} brothers said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Leave this place and go to Judea, so that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples there can also see the works {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are doing.
en.R: His brothers said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "You should leave here and go to Judea. Then {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples there can see the things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are doing too.

es.L: Le dijeron, pues, sus hermanos: «Sal de aquí y vete a Judea, para que también tus discípulos vean las obras que haces;
es.B: Entonces sus hermanos le dijeron: «Deja este lugar y vete a Judea, para que tus discípulos de allí también vean las obras que haces.
es.R: Sus hermanos le dijeron: «Deberías irte de aquí e ir a Judea. Así tus discípulos de allí también podrán ver las cosas que haces.

decisions.choice: brothers: the brothers of Jesus named in 2:12
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary one for brothers; specific men are meant, and Mark 6:3 names four of them (James, Joses, Judas and Simon). Christians differ on who they were: younger sons of Mary and Joseph, sons of Joseph by an earlier marriage, or close relatives such as cousins. The text does not settle it, so every level says "brothers".

decisions.choice: your disciples: followers of Jesus in Judea and Jerusalem
alternatives: the disciples who had turned back in 6:66
decisions.reason: Jesus had gained many followers in Jerusalem and Judea before (2:23; 3:22-26; 4:1), and the brothers speak as though they need to see him at work there. Another view is that they mean the disciples who had stopped following him (6:66), who might be won back by a public show. The text does not say which.

decisions.choice: the brothers urge a public display at the festival
decisions.reason: The festival was the time when the crowds would be in Jerusalem (7:2). The brothers want Jesus to do his works where they will be seen and win him a following. John explains in 7:5 that they did not believe in him; their advice is like the crowd's wish to make him king (6:15), a way of being great that Jesus refuses.

decisions.choice: there (B, R); the things you are doing (R)
decisions.reason: "There" makes plain that the disciples meant are those in Judea (meaning decision m2). Readable says "the things you are doing" for "your works", here and at 7:7, so the link between the two verses stays in plain words.

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: Specific men are meant, Jesus's brothers (2:12), so the gender setting does not apply.

decisions.choice: de allí
decisions.reason: As in English: the disciples meant are those in Judea (meaning decision m2).

source.text: οὐδεὶς γάρ τι ἐν κρυπτῷ ποιεῖ καὶ ζητεῖ αὐτὸς ἐν παρρησίᾳ εἶναι· εἰ ταῦτα ποιεῖς, φανέρωσον σεαυτὸν τῷ κόσμῳ.

records.literal_gloss: For no one anything in secret does and seeks himself in openness to be; if these things you do, reveal yourself to the world."

en.L: For no one does anything in secret and himself seeks to be [known] openly. If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do these things, show {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} to the world."
en.B: No one who wants to be known openly does things in secret. If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are doing these things, show {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} to the world."
en.R: People who want to be known do not hide what they do. If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are doing these things, show {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} to the whole world."

es.L: Porque nadie hace algo en secreto y a la vez procura darse a conocer abiertamente. Si haces estas cosas, manifiéstate al mundo».
es.B: Nadie que quiera darse a conocer abiertamente hace las cosas en secreto. Si de verdad haces estas cosas, muéstrate al mundo».
es.R: Quien quiere que lo conozcan no esconde lo que hace. Si de verdad haces estas cosas, muéstrate a todo el mundo».

decisions.choice: openly: in public view, known to everyone
decisions.reason: παρρησίᾳ means openness: speaking freely and plainly, or acting where all can see. Here it is set against "in secret". The word runs through the chapter: no one speaks openly about Jesus for fear (7:13), and then he teaches openly in the temple (7:26). Elsewhere it means plain speech (10:24; 11:14; 16:25, 29), and at his trial Jesus says he has spoken openly to the world (18:20).

decisions.choice: show yourself to the world: make yourself known to the public
decisions.reason: The verb φανέρωσον means to make visible or reveal. John uses it of Jesus revealing his glory at Cana (2:11), and the brothers mean something similar but on their own terms: a public display. The same root returns in 7:10, where Jesus goes up not publicly but as it were in secret, and the phrase "in secret" is repeated there as well.

decisions.choice: the world: people at large, the public
decisions.reason: In the brothers' mouth "the world" means everyone, all who will be in Jerusalem for the feast. Jesus answers in 7:7 with the darker sense of the word: the world that hates him.

decisions.choice: if you do these things: granting that he does them, with an edge of challenge
alternatives: since you do these things, with no challenge
decisions.reason: The brothers do not doubt that Jesus does works; the condition assumes it. But John adds at once that they did not believe in him (7:5), so the words also carry a challenge: if he is what his works suggest, let him prove it before everyone.

decisions.choice: openly
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "openly" here and in 7:13 for the same word, so the thread of the chapter shows. Literal supplies "known", which the Greek implies. Readable says "want to be known" and keeps "openly" for 7:13.

decisions.choice: abiertamente
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "abiertamente" here and in 7:13 for the same word, so the thread of the chapter shows; 7:10 has a different word, "públicamente".

source.text: οὐδὲ γὰρ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπίστευον εἰς αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: For not even the brothers of him were believing in him.

en.L: For not even {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} brothers were believing in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: For even {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own brothers did not believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Even {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own brothers did not believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Porque ni siquiera sus hermanos creían en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Porque ni siquiera sus propios hermanos creían en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Ni siquiera sus propios hermanos creían en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

decisions.choice: for: John explains why the brothers spoke as they did
decisions.reason: The sentence is the narrator's comment on 7:3-4. The brothers' advice is not the advice of believers. "Not even" shows how far the unbelief reached: his own family was not convinced.

decisions.choice: were not believing in him: they did not yet trust him as the one sent from God
alternatives: they had never believed and never would
decisions.reason: The tense describes their state at that time. They knew of his works and wanted them shown, but that is not the believing John writes for (20:31). It did not stay so: after the resurrection his brothers are with the disciples in prayer (Acts 1:14), the risen Jesus appeared to James (1 Corinthians 15:7), and James became a leader of the church in Jerusalem (Galatians 1:19; Acts 15:13). Compare Mark 3:21, where his family tries to take charge of him.

decisions.choice: own
decisions.reason: "His own brothers" brings out the force of "not even" (meaning decision m1).

source.text: λέγει οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ὁ καιρὸς ὁ ἐμὸς οὔπω πάρεστιν, ὁ δὲ καιρὸς ὁ ὑμέτερος πάντοτέ ἐστιν ἕτοιμος.

records.literal_gloss: Says therefore to them the Jesus, "The time the mine not yet is present, but the time the yours always is ready.

en.L: So Jesus says to them, "My time is not yet here, but your time is always ready.
en.B: So Jesus told them, "My time has not yet arrived, but for you the time is always right.
en.R: Jesus answered, "It is not yet the right time for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. But for you, any time is right.

es.L: Les dice, pues, Jesús: «Mi tiempo aún no ha llegado, pero {{plural_you:el tiempo de ustedes|vuestro tiempo}} siempre está a mano.
es.B: Entonces Jesús les dijo: «Mi tiempo todavía no ha llegado, pero para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} cualquier momento es bueno.
es.R: Jesús les respondió: «Todavía no es el momento oportuno para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Pero para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} cualquier momento es bueno.

decisions.choice: my time: the right moment, set by the Father, for Jesus to act and to be revealed
alternatives: the hour of his death only
simply the right day to travel
decisions.reason: καιρὸς means the fitting or appointed moment rather than a span of time. It is a different word from "hour", which John uses for the hour of Jesus's death and glory (2:4; 7:30; 8:20; 12:23; 13:1), but the thought is close: as at Cana (2:4), Jesus will not act on someone else's timing. Here the nearest sense is the time to go up and show himself publicly, but the words look further, to the time when he will be revealed to the world on the cross and in his rising.

decisions.choice: your time is always ready: the brothers have nothing to wait for
decisions.reason: They may go to the festival whenever they like, because nothing hangs on it and the world has no quarrel with them (7:7). Jesus lives by the Father's timing (5:19, 30); they do not.

decisions.choice: not yet: the time will come
decisions.reason: "Not yet" points ahead. The same words return in 7:8 and in the narrator's remark that his hour had not yet come (7:30; 8:20).

decisions.choice: told (B); answered (R)
decisions.reason: John often tells a story in the present tense ("says") for vividness. Literal keeps the present; Balanced and Readable use the past, as stories are normally told in this language. This applies to every such verb in the passage.

decisions.choice: time (L, B, R); the right time (R)
decisions.reason: "Time" at every level, never "hour", so a reader can tell this word from the one the book's terms render "hour" (2:4; 7:30). Readable says "the right time" to show that a fitting moment is meant (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal; pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John: Literal keeps John's present ("dice", "ven"); Balanced and Readable use the pretérito. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: tiempo, momento oportuno; never hora
decisions.reason: This is a different word from the "hour" of 2:4 and 7:30 (meaning decision m1), so Spanish never says "hora" for it; a reader can tell the two apart.

source.text: οὐ δύναται ὁ κόσμος μισεῖν ὑμᾶς, ἐμὲ δὲ μισεῖ, ὅτι ἐγὼ μαρτυρῶ περὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ πονηρά ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: Not is able the world to hate you, but me it hates, because I testify about it that the works of it evil are.

en.L: The world cannot hate you, but it hates {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, because I testify about it that its works are evil.
en.B: The world cannot hate you, but it hates {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, because I testify that its works are evil.
en.R: The world has no reason to hate you. But it hates {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, because I keep telling it that the things it does are evil.

es.L: El mundo no puede odiar{{plural_you:los|os}} a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, pero a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} me odia, porque yo doy testimonio acerca de él de que sus obras son malas.
es.B: El mundo no puede odiar{{plural_you:los|os}} a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, pero a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} me odia, porque doy testimonio de que sus obras son malas.
es.R: El mundo no tiene por qué odiar{{plural_you:los|os}}. Pero a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} me odia, porque le digo una y otra vez que lo que hace es malo.

decisions.choice: the world: humanity organized against God
alternatives: people at large, the public (as in 7:4)
decisions.reason: In 7:4 the brothers meant the public. Jesus takes up the word in its darker sense: people as they turn away from God and resist the light (1:10; 3:19-20; 15:18-19; 17:14). The world cannot hate the brothers because they belong to it; they share its outlook.

decisions.choice: I testify that its works are evil: his witness exposes what the world does
decisions.reason: Testimony is one of John's great themes (1:7; 5:31-39). The thought matches 3:19-20: people love darkness because their works are evil, and they hate the light that shows it. The brothers asked Jesus to show his works to the world (7:3); he answers that his witness shows up the world's works.

decisions.choice: cannot hate you: there is no reason for it to
alternatives: the world is unable to hate anyone good
decisions.reason: "Cannot" does not mean the brothers are good; it means the world sees nothing in them to oppose. Jesus says the same to his disciples in reverse: because he chose them out of the world, the world hates them (15:19).

decisions.choice: I keep telling it ... the things it does
decisions.reason: Readable uses the present of ongoing action for "testify" and says "the things it does" for "its works", matching 7:3 at that level.

decisions.choice: le digo una y otra vez ... lo que hace
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable shows ongoing testimony and says "lo que hace" for "its works".

source.text: ὑμεῖς ἀνάβητε εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν· ἐγὼ οὐκ ἀναβαίνω εἰς τὴν ἑορτὴν ταύτην, ὅτι ὁ ἐμὸς καιρὸς οὔπω πεπλήρωται.

records.literal_gloss: You go up to the feast; I not am going up to the feast this, because the my time not yet has been fulfilled."

en.L: You go up to the feast. I am not going up to this feast, because {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} time has not yet been fulfilled."
en.B: You go up to the festival. I am not going up to this festival, because {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} time has not yet fully come."
en.R: You go up to Jerusalem for the festival. I am not going to this festival, because it is not yet the right time for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

es.L: {{plural_you:Suban ustedes|Subid vosotros}} a la fiesta. Yo no subo a esta fiesta, porque mi tiempo aún no se ha cumplido».
es.B: {{plural_you:Suban ustedes|Subid vosotros}} a la fiesta. Yo no voy a subir a esta fiesta, porque mi tiempo todavía no ha llegado del todo».
es.R: {{plural_you:Vayan ustedes|Id vosotros}} a Jerusalén para la fiesta. Yo no voy a esta fiesta, porque todavía no es el momento oportuno para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}».

decisions.choice: I am not going up (SBLGNT)
alternatives: I am not yet going up (many manuscripts, including P66, P75 and Vaticanus)
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads οὐκ, "not". Many manuscripts, among them the early papyri P66 and P75 and Codex Vaticanus, read οὔπω, "not yet", the word used at the end of the verse. "Not" is found in Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Bezae and early Latin and Syriac versions. Because "not" seems to clash with 7:10, where Jesus does go up, it is easy to see why a copyist would change it to "not yet" and hard to see why anyone would change "not yet" to "not"; this is why the SBLGNT prefers it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: I am not going up: not now, and not in the way the brothers ask
decisions.reason: Jesus goes up a few days later (7:10), so his words are not a flat refusal for all time. Three explanations are given, and they can stand together. First, the present tense means "I am not going up now", with his brothers' party. Second, he refuses the public display they asked for (7:4); when he does go, it is not publicly but as it were in secret (7:10). Third, "go up" is also John's word for Jesus going up to the Father (3:13; 6:62; 20:17): at this feast he will not "go up" in that sense, for his time is not yet fulfilled. The text does not say which is uppermost.

decisions.choice: go up: travel to Jerusalem for the festival
decisions.reason: Jerusalem stands on high ground, and pilgrims spoke of going up to it for the feasts (Psalm 122:4; John 2:13; 5:1).

decisions.choice: has not yet been fulfilled: the time is not yet full
decisions.reason: The verb pictures a measure being filled up: the time the Father has set is not yet complete. It echoes "not yet" in 7:6.

decisions.choice: has not yet fully come (B); it is not yet the right time for me (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the idea of fullness in everyday words; Readable says it as in 7:6. Literal keeps "fulfilled". Balanced and Readable say "festival", as in 7:2.

decisions.choice: to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable names the place that "go up" implies (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: no se ha cumplido (L); no ha llegado del todo (B)
decisions.reason: As in English: the time is not yet full (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: a Jerusalén
decisions.reason: Readable names the place that "subir" implies (meaning decision m3).

source.text: ταῦτα δὲ εἰπὼν αὐτὸς ἔμεινεν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: These things and having said, he remained in the Galilee.

en.L: And having said these things, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} remained in Galilee.
en.B: After saying this, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stayed on in Galilee.
en.R: After Jesus said this, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stayed in Galilee.

es.L: Y habiéndoles dicho esto, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se quedó en Galilea.
es.B: Después de decir esto, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se quedó en Galilea.
es.R: Después de decir esto, Jesús se quedó en Galilea.

decisions.choice: he himself: Jesus, in contrast to his brothers
alternatives: having said these things to them (some manuscripts)
decisions.reason: The pronoun is stressed: the brothers go, but Jesus stays. Some manuscripts read "to them" ("having said these things to them") instead; the sense is not changed. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: remained: stayed on, in the ordinary sense
decisions.reason: This is John's verb "remain", but here it has its everyday sense of staying in a place (as in 1:39 and 2:12), not the deeper sense of remaining in Jesus (6:56; 15:4).

decisions.choice: stayed on (B); stayed (R)
decisions.reason: The book's terms keep "remain" for the theological sense and use the natural word in ordinary senses. Literal keeps "remained".

decisions.choice: se quedó
decisions.reason: John's verb "remain" in its everyday sense of staying in a place (meaning decision m2), so Spanish says "quedarse", as at 1:39 and 4:40, keeping "permanecer" for the weighty sense.

source.text: Ὡς δὲ ἀνέβησαν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν, τότε καὶ αὐτὸς ἀνέβη, οὐ φανερῶς ἀλλὰ ὡς ἐν κρυπτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: But when went up the brothers of him to the feast, then also he went up, not openly but as in secret.

en.L: But when {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} brothers had gone up to the feast, then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also went up, not publicly but as [it were] in secret.
en.B: But after {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} brothers had gone up to the festival, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went up too, not publicly but in secret, as it were.
en.R: But after {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} brothers had left for the festival, Jesus went too. He did not travel where people could see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He went almost in secret.

es.L: Pero cuando sus hermanos habían subido a la fiesta, entonces también {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} subió, no públicamente, sino como en secreto.
es.B: Pero cuando sus hermanos ya habían subido a la fiesta, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} también subió, no públicamente, sino como en secreto.
es.R: Pero cuando sus hermanos ya se habían ido a la fiesta, Jesús también fue. No viajó a la vista de la gente. Fue casi en secreto.

decisions.choice: as it were in secret (SBLGNT)
alternatives: in secret (some witnesses, among them Sinaiticus and Bezae)
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts, among them P66, P75 and Codex Vaticanus, have the small word "as", which softens the phrase: he went more or less in secret. Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Bezae and some early Latin copies leave it out, reading simply "in secret". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: not publicly but in secret: the opposite of what the brothers asked
decisions.reason: "Publicly" is from the same root as "show yourself" in 7:4, and "in secret" repeats the brothers' own phrase. They told him that no one acts in secret who wants to be known; he goes up, but not to show himself to the world.

decisions.choice: then he also went up: on his own timing, not at his brothers' bidding
decisions.reason: Going up after the brothers is not a broken word (see the note at 7:8). As at Cana, where Jesus first said his hour had not come and then acted (2:4-7), he acts when the Father's time allows, and in his own way. In the middle of the feast he will teach openly in the temple (7:14, 26).

decisions.choice: publicly
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "openly" for the different word of 7:4 and 7:13, and say "publicly" here so the two words stay distinct.

decisions.choice: He did not travel where people could see him. He went almost in secret.
decisions.reason: Readable spells out "not publicly" in a short sentence and gives the softening "as it were" as "almost".

decisions.choice: públicamente
decisions.reason: A different word from the "abiertamente" of 7:4 and 7:13, so it gets a different Spanish word. Literal needs no bracket for "como".

source.text: οἱ οὖν Ἰουδαῖοι ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ καὶ ἔλεγον· Ποῦ ἐστιν ἐκεῖνος;

records.literal_gloss: The therefore Jews were seeking him at the feast and were saying, "Where is that one?"

en.L: So the Jews were seeking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} at the feast and were saying, "Where is that one?"
en.B: So the Jewish leaders were looking for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} at the festival, asking, "Where is that man?"
en.R: At the festival the Jewish leaders kept looking for Jesus. They kept asking, "Where is that man?"

es.L: Los judíos, pues, lo buscaban en la fiesta y decían: «¿Dónde está aquel?».
es.B: Los dirigentes judíos lo buscaban en la fiesta y preguntaban: «¿Dónde está ese hombre?».
es.R: En la fiesta, los dirigentes judíos seguían buscando a Jesús. Preguntaban una y otra vez: «¿Dónde está ese hombre?».

decisions.choice: the Jews: the religious authorities in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: They are distinct from the crowds of 7:12, who are afraid of them (7:13), and their search picks up 7:1, where they were seeking to kill him. It is the leadership, not the Jewish people as a whole: the pilgrims at the feast are Jews too.

decisions.choice: that one: they avoid using his name
decisions.reason: ἐκεῖνος; is a pointing word, "that one". Their not naming him keeps him at a distance and may carry contempt (compare 9:12, 28).

decisions.choice: were seeking him: a hostile search
decisions.reason: The tense pictures a search that went on during the feast. John uses the same verb for seeking to kill Jesus (5:18; 7:1, 19, 25); in 7:34-36 Jesus will tell them that they will seek him and not find him.

decisions.choice: the Jewish leaders
decisions.reason: Where the word means the authorities, Balanced and Readable name them (see the book's terms). The footnote gives the word John wrote.

decisions.choice: that man
decisions.reason: "That man" carries the same distance as the Greek in natural English. Literal keeps "that one".

decisions.choice: los judíos (L); los dirigentes judíos (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the religious authorities in Jerusalem (meaning decision m1), so Balanced and Readable name them, as at 5:10-18. The word John wrote is "los judíos".

decisions.choice: ese hombre (B, R); aquel (L)
decisions.reason: As in English: keeps the distance of the Greek pointing word (meaning decision m2).

source.text: καὶ γογγυσμὸς περὶ αὐτοῦ ἦν πολὺς ἐν τοῖς ὄχλοις· οἱ μὲν ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἀγαθός ἐστιν, ἄλλοι δὲ ἔλεγον· Οὔ, ἀλλὰ πλανᾷ τὸν ὄχλον.

records.literal_gloss: And muttering about him there was much among the crowds; some were saying, "Good he is," but others were saying, "No, but he leads astray the crowd."

en.L: And there was much muttering about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} among the crowds. Some were saying, "He is good," but others were saying, "No, rather {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} leads the crowd astray."
en.B: Among the crowds there was a great deal of muttering about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Some said, "He is a good man." Others said, "No, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is leading the people astray."
en.R: People in the crowds were whispering about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Some said, "He is a good man." Others said, "No, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is fooling the people and leading them away from God."

es.L: Y había mucha murmuración acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} entre las multitudes. Unos decían: «Es bueno»; pero otros decían: «No, sino que engaña a la multitud».
es.B: Entre la multitud había mucha murmuración acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Unos decían: «Es un hombre bueno». Otros decían: «No, está engañando al pueblo».
es.R: La gente hablaba en voz baja acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Unos decían: «Es un hombre bueno». Otros decían: «No, engaña a la gente y la aparta de Dios».

decisions.choice: muttering: low-voiced talk among the people
decisions.reason: γογγυσμὸς is the noun from the verb for the grumbling of 6:41 and 6:43, which echoes Israel's grumbling in the wilderness. Here the talk is not all complaint, since some speak in Jesus's favor: it is talk under the breath, kept quiet for fear (7:13). In 7:32 the Pharisees hear the crowd muttering these things.

decisions.choice: he leads the crowd astray: the charge against a false prophet
alternatives: an ordinary charge of misleading people
decisions.reason: πλανᾷ means to lead astray or deceive. Deuteronomy 13:1-11 warns against a prophet who does signs and wonders but leads the people away from the LORD, and orders that such a person be put to death. The charge is serious: it would make Jesus deserving of death. The Pharisees use the same verb in 7:47, and in Matthew 27:63 the chief priests call Jesus "that deceiver".

decisions.choice: he is good: an honest and upright man
decisions.reason: The verdict is favorable but limited: a good man, not the Christ or the prophet. It is not the believing John is calling for, and in 7:13 even these people keep their opinion quiet.

decisions.choice: among the crowds: the many groups of pilgrims at the feast
decisions.reason: The plural pictures the city full of pilgrims from many places. The singular "the crowd" at the end of the verse speaks of the people in general.

decisions.choice: muttering (L, B); whispering (R)
decisions.reason: "Grumbling" in 6:41 fit people who were complaining; here the talk includes praise, so Literal and Balanced say "muttering", which keeps the sound of the word and its link with 6:41 without implying that all of it was complaint. Readable says "whispering".

decisions.choice: is leading the people astray (B); is fooling the people and leading them away from God (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "the people", since the crowd as a whole is meant. Readable explains what leading astray means in this charge: turning people away from God (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps "leads the crowd astray".

decisions.choice: murmuración (L, B); hablaba en voz baja (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish "murmurar" covers both complaining and talking in low voices, so Literal and Balanced keep the word of 6:41-43 (meaning decision m1), where English has to change to "muttering".

decisions.choice: engaña a la gente y la aparta de Dios
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable explains what leading astray means here (meaning decision m2).

source.text: οὐδεὶς μέντοι παρρησίᾳ ἐλάλει περὶ αὐτοῦ διὰ τὸν φόβον τῶν Ἰουδαίων.

records.literal_gloss: No one however openly was speaking about him because of the fear of the Jews.

en.L: However, no one was speaking openly about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} because of the fear of the Jews.
en.B: Yet no one would speak openly about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because they were afraid of the Jewish leaders.
en.R: But no one dared to talk about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} openly, because they were afraid of the Jewish leaders.

es.L: Sin embargo, nadie hablaba abiertamente de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} por miedo a los judíos.
es.B: Pero nadie hablaba abiertamente de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, porque tenían miedo de los dirigentes judíos.
es.R: Pero nadie se atrevía a hablar de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} abiertamente, porque tenían miedo de los dirigentes judíos.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the religious authorities in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The people who are afraid are themselves Jews, so the word cannot mean the Jewish people here. It means those in power, as in 7:11 and in the other places where people fear "the Jews": the parents of the man born blind (9:22), the rulers who believed in secret (12:42), Joseph of Arimathea (19:38), and the disciples after the crucifixion (20:19).

decisions.choice: openly: freely and in public
decisions.reason: παρρησίᾳ is the word the brothers used in 7:4. They told Jesus to be known openly; instead, no one dares even to speak of him openly. Both his friends and his opponents speak under their breath (7:12).

decisions.choice: the fear of the Jews: the fear people had of the authorities
alternatives: the fear felt by the Jewish leaders
decisions.reason: The phrase means the people's fear of the leaders, not a fear the leaders felt. The tense of "was speaking" describes how things stood throughout the feast.

decisions.choice: they were afraid of the Jewish leaders
alternatives: because of the fear of the Jews (Literal)
decisions.reason: Where the word means the authorities, Balanced and Readable name them (see the book's terms). The footnote gives the word John wrote. Balanced and Readable turn "the fear of" into a verb, which is the natural way to say it.

decisions.choice: los judíos (L); los dirigentes judíos (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the religious authorities in Jerusalem (meaning decision m1), so Balanced and Readable name them, as at 5:10-18. The word John wrote is "los judíos".
